title: Find the Union
stepTitle: Solve Problems on Arrays [Easy -> Medium -> Hard]
category: Solve Problems on Arrays [Easy -> Medium -> Hard]
problemStatement: Return the sorted union of two sorted arrays (each value once).
intuition: Both inputs are sorted, so a merge walk sees equal values side by side; you never need a hash set.

approaches.title: Brute: set union then sort
approaches.idea: Correct, but discards the sorted precondition.
approaches.code:
def union_set(a: list[int], b: list[int]) -> list[int]:
    return sorted(set(a) | set(b))

approaches.title: Optimal: two-pointer merge
approaches.idea: Advance the smaller side; append only when different from the last appended value.
approaches.dryRun:
a=[1,2], b=[2,3]
push 1; push 2; b[0]=2 duplicate skipped; push 3 -> [1,2,3]
approaches.whyWorks: Sorted order means all copies of a value are contiguous in the merged stream.

commonMistakes: Dropping the leftover tail of one array
De-duplicating only across arrays, not within
patternRecognition: Two sorted sequences -> merge walk, never a hash set
followUps: Do it in-place when a has spare capacity
interviewInsight: Proposing a set is an instant signal that you ignored the "sorted" in the prompt.
